 CORAM:HONOURABLE MS. JUSTICE VAIBHAVI D. NANAVATI  Date : 18/01/2023  ORAL JUDGMENT 1.
The present Appeal is filed by the appellants - original claimants seeking enhancement of the compensation amount awarded by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Aux.)

NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1647/2020 JUDGMENT DATED: 18/01/2023 undefined (hereinafter referred to as "the Tribunal") vide impugned judgment and award dated 26.06.2019 passed in M.A.C.P. No.56 of 2005, whereby the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition and awarded a sum of Rs.9,47,500/- at the interest rate of 9% p.a.
The appellants herein are the legal heirs of deceased - Babu Naran Marand, who was aged 48 years at the time of accident.

2. Brief facts of the present case are that, on 06.01.2005, the deceased - Babu Naran Marand (Ahir)
was proceedings from Anjar to Chandroda on Motorcycle, bearing registration No.GJ-12-E-5114.
He was driving the said motorcycle on the left side of the road with moderate speed.

When he reached near village : Bhuvad, at around 8:00 hrs., the driver of one Tanker, bearing registration No.MH-04-BU-3676 had come from opposite direction driving the said tanker in rash and negligent manner, with excessive speed and without observing the traffic rules.
As a result of which, the driver lost control on the tanker and the said tanker came on the wrong side of the road and collided with the motorcycle.
The deceased sustained serious injuries and died on the spot.
The death of the deceased was direct result of the negligence of the driver of the tanker.

2.1 The claimants had filed a petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 for the compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- together with costs and interest at the rate of 12% p.a. from the date of filing of the claim petition i.e. 05.02.2005.
The Tribunal after considering the documents on record awarded a compensation to the tune of Rs.9,47,500/-
NEUTRAL
CITATION C/FA/1647/2020 JUDGMENT DATED: 18/01/2023 undefined along with interest @ 9% p.a. from the date of filing of the claim petition till its realization.
2.2 The appellants - original claimants, being aggrieved by the compensation awarded by the Tribunal, approached this Court by way of present appeal.

3. Heard Mr. Hemal Shah, the learned advocate appearing for the appellants and Mr. Ajay Mehta,
the learned advocate appearing for the respondent No.2- Insurance Company.
4.

Mr. Hemal Shah, the learned advocate appearing for the appellants, submitted that Tribunal has erred in considering the documentary evidence, which was produce on record to show that the deceased was earning Rs.54,000/- per month from the multiple business of (1) transport operator in the name and style of "Shree Pithad Transport" (2) Business of Radiator repairing in the name and Rajesh Babu Marand (Ahir) vs Satnamsingh C Singh on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39719682/
2 style of "Jay Yadav Radiator" and (3) Agriculture work.

sentences.text: Mr. Shah, the learned advocate, also submitted that the Tribunal has erred in considering the income of the deceased on the lower side i.e. only Rs.6000/- per month.

Mr. Shah, the learned advocate, further submitted that the loss of consortium which has been considered by the Tribunal is considered only qua the claimants,
however, the consortium is required to be considered qua the legal heirs i.e. minors appellant Nos.4 and 5 and therefore, the said amount is required to be granted.
6.

Per contra, Mr. Ajay Mehta, the learned advocate appearing for the respondent No.2 - Insurance Company, NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1647/2020 JUDGMENT DATED: 18/01/2023 undefined submitted that the appellants herein have failed to produce on record any income record to show that the deceased was earning Rs.54,000/- per month.

Mr. Mehta, the learned advocate, also referred to the evidence that is produced on record and submitted that all the record with regard to the income, which has been produced by the appellants, is prior to 1997.

The last income record produce by the claimants is of the year 1997 and the untoward incident occurred in the year 2005 and between the said period, there is no record to show that the deceased was earning Rs.54,000/-
per month.
Mr. Mehta, the learned advocate was not in a position to controvert to the rest of the submissions advanced by Mr. Shah, the learned advocate appearing for the appellants.

7. At this stage, it is apposite to refer to the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of United India Insurance Company Limited Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur & Ors., reported in (2021) 11 SCC 780, wherein it has held as under:
"29.

entities.text: United India Insurance Company Limited Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur & Ors., reported in (2021) 11 SCC 780
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Loss of Consortium, in legal parlance, was historically given a narrow meaning to be awarded only to the spouse i.e. the right of the spouse to the company, care,
help, comfort, guidance, society, solace, affection and sexual relations with his or her mate.
The loss of companionship, love, care and protection, etc., the spouse is entitled to get, has to be compensated appropriately.
The concept of non- pecuniary damage for loss of consortium is one of the major heads for awarding compensation in various jurisdictions such as the United States of America, Australia, etc.
English courts have recognised the right of a spouse to get compensation even during the period of temporary disablement.

30. In Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Nanu Ram, this Court interpreted "consortium" to be a compendious term, which encompasses spousal consortium,
parental consortium, as well as filial consortium.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Nanu Ram
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The right to consortium would include the company, care, help, comfort, guidance, solace and affection of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1647/2020 JUDGMENT DATED: 18/01/2023 undefined the deceased, which is a loss to his family.
With respect to a spouse, it would include sexual relations with the deceased spouse.

31. Parental consortium is granted to the child upon the premature death of a parent,
for loss of parental aid, protection, affection, society, discipline, guidance and training.
Filial consortium is the right of the parents to compensation in the case of an accidental death of a child.

An accident leading to the death of a child causes great Rajesh Babu Marand (Ahir) vs Satnamsingh C Singh on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39719682/
3 shock and agony to the parents and family of the deceased.

entities.text: Rajesh Babu Marand (Ahir) vs Satnamsingh C Singh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The greatest agony for a parent is to lose their child during their lifetime.
Children are valued for their love and affection, and their role in the family unit.
32. Modern jurisdictions world-over have recognized that the value of a child's consortium far exceeds the economic value of the compensation awarded in the case of the death of a child.
Most jurisdictions permit parents to be awarded compensation under loss of consortium on the death of a child.
The amount awarded to the parents is the compensation for loss of love and affection, care and companionship of the deceased child.
33. The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is a beneficial legislation which has been framed with the object of providing relief to the victims, or their families, in cases of genuine claims.
In case where a parent has lost their minor child, or unmarried son or daughter, the parents are entitled to be awarded loss of consortium under the head of Filial Consortium.
Parental Consortium is awarded to the children who lose the care and protection of their parents in motor vehicle accidents.
The amount to be awarded for loss consortium will be as per the amount fixed in Pranay Sethi (supra).
34. At this stage, we consider it necessary to provide uniformity with respect to the grant of consortium, and loss of love and affection.
Several Tribunals and High Courts have been awarding compensation for both loss of consortium and loss of love and affection.
The Constitution Bench in Pranay Sethi (supra), has recognized only three conventional heads under which compensation can be awarded viz. loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses.
In Magma General (supra), this Court gave a comprehensive interpretation to consortium to include spousal consortium, parental consortium, as well as filial consortium.
Loss of love and affection is comprehended in loss of consortium.
35. The Tribunals and High Courts are directed to award compensation for loss of consortium, which is a legitimate conventional head.

There is no justification to award compensation towards loss of love and affection as a separate head."
8.

Considering the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1647/2020 JUDGMENT DATED: 18/01/2023 undefined Court in the case of Sarla Verma and others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in [2009] 6 SCC 121 and in case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, reported in [2017] 16 SCC 680, the compensation is to be awarded just and adequate and for that the principles enumerated in the said judgments is required to be born in mind at the time of determining the amount of compensation.

Smt. Somwati and others, (2020) 9 SCC 644 and United India Insurance Company Limited Vs.
Satinder Kaur alias Satwinder Kaur and others, AIR 2020 SC 3076, the appellants are also entitled to receive the amount under the head of consortium.

The income is enhanced by Rs.4,000/- i.e. total Rs.10,000/-.
The loss of consortium is enhanced by Rs.80,000/-.

(i) Appeal is allowed in part.
